issue.title: test_pushed_and_popped_screens_release_their_views times out in the broad lane but passes on identical source
issue.description:
Relayed by sase-1ou.6.land--2 from sase-1ou.6.1 note #4. In check d25f8e01bb088e19fb5eee04ec5f2c79 (Python 3.14.7 / Textual 8.0.1, broad lane with one worker), tests/pager/test_view_leak.py::test_pushed_and_popped_screens_release_their_views failed waiting 5.0 seconds for all PagerView weakrefs to die. Triage classified it KNOWN using independent witness 01564beb93f5085605d33a22bce43f1f. The check source was base 89c40e30b004255e71f678dfe5b90f5741afca02 plus five Files-navigation files.

The lander reconstructed that exact tracked source from git archive, overlaid all five dirty files from 2e68053dab, and verified their SHA256 hashes against both before/after ToolRun fingerprints. The failing node passed in isolation on this same source: 1 passed in 20.17s (test call 1.35s). Current master 2e68053dab also passes all three view-leak tests. This establishes one broad-lane failure and one isolated same-source pass; the long-run failure rate is unknown. The reconstructed source uses a separate process and the lander venv, not the original broad-suite process state.

Investigate retained PagerView references and teardown ordering under the broad lane. Do not increase the 5s timeout or weaken the lifetime assertions. Root cause is unproven, so size large. PagerView does not inherit SectionViewMixin and the Files repair changed no pager code. All-status exact/related searches and the recent-task sweep found no matching report. Reviewed active-epic inventory and the plausible GC epic sase-1nf.14.1; no credible causal link was established, including no evidence for assuming sase-j7 process-global state leakage.
